text.brief: On December 10, 2010, the Nobel Committee placed Liu Xiaobo's diploma on an empty chair in Oslo.
text.record: Liu had helped write Charter 08, a call for constitutional government that more than ten thousand people signed, and a court sentenced him to eleven years for inciting subversion ([CECC: Beijing court sentences Liu Xiaobo to 11 years (January 5, 2010)](https://www.cecc.gov/publications/commission-analysis/beijing-court-sentences-liu-xiaobo-to-11-years); [The Nobel Peace Prize 2010: speed read](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2010/speedread/)). The Party pressed governments to stay away from the ceremony, and about eighteen did. It froze relations with Norway for six years and held his wife Liu Xia under house arrest without charge. Liu died in custody of liver cancer on July 13, 2017 ([The Nobel Peace Prize 2010: Liu Xiaobo, facts](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2010/xiaobo/facts/)).
text.reading: The Party jailed a writer for a document and then punished a country for a prize its government did not award, which is Stratagem 26. The empty chair became the image of the prize, and the Party never let Liu leave to fill it.
text.gapText: Architecture Governance. No alliance owned the response when the Party punished Norway, so one small country carried the cost of a shared value alone.
text.fix: Answer the economic punishment of one ally for a shared value with a shared response, agreed in advance.
